summary: The production constrained-HTTP write-authority constructor resolves an exact signed workspace activation from a separately persisted customer-local trust ledger; rotation, revocation, expiry and local consumption fail closed, while signed restore atomically publishes audit-only state that requires a fresh post-restore activation.
boundaries: The frozen claim covers one local fictional constrained-HTTP authority path using SQLite and an independently pinned customer-local trust configuration.
The production constructor excludes caller-supplied admin keys, activation receipts and test clocks; the separately exported test-only constructor remains outside the production claim.
Signed restore publishes only audit-only state and requires a strictly post-restore signed activation before authority can resolve.
Normal crash/restart and local multi-process SQLite serialization are covered; privileged raw-file rollback requires an external monotonic anchor and is not resisted or claimed.
HSM or OS-keychain custody, distributed consensus, multi-host authority, customer use, production reliability, arbitrary APIs and public evidence are not claimed.
freezeRule: Any change to a listed file requires a new checkpoint and regenerated hashes.
